policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וּבִדְבָרְךָ֣ is singular (Ncmsc); ketiv ובדבריך is plural (Ncmpc). ASV closes the verse “that I have done all these things at thy word” — singular “word”, where the plural of this same noun is rendered “the words of the prophets” at 1 Kings 22:13. The singular distinguishes the qere.

Qere בִּרְכָּֽיו and ketiv ברכו are the same dual of בֶּרֶךְ with a 3ms suffix; OSHB tags both Ncfdc/Sp3ms, so the ketiv is only the defective spelling. ASV “put his face between his knees” renders either, and no note is mapped to the word, so nothing distinguishes them.
